newsitem.title: UK: Dry bulk shipping rates seen stronger this summer.
newsitem.headline: Dry bulk shipping rates seen stronger this summer.

text.p: UK shipbroking group Simpson Spence and Young (SSY) has forecast that dry bulk shipping markets will remain competitive over the summer and that rates will not fall as low as they did in the middle of 1996.

In its monthly report for May, SSY said prospects over the next few months are likely to be influenced by seasonal factors during the traditionally quieter summer period, but that the market would remain more robust than last year.
"The volume of business to be concluded remains huge and the competition fierce," SSY said.
"If shipowners sit back and just wait for things to happen they will not be optimising their strategies," the London-based broker stated.
SSY added that if charterers were waiting for the market to fall to the depths hit in mid-1996, they might be mistaken.
"That particular trough seems less likely to be reached - despite the fact that current rates are lower than the same time last year," it said.
SSY attributed greater market robustness particularly to firm expectations for the trade in steam coal this year and next. -Paul Berrill Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087. Fax 5017.
